question: Do singular directions inside bias-augmented attention and MLP weight matrices provide sparse, interpretable, and causally meaningful subcomponent units for transformer circuits beyond whole heads and layers?

key_findings.claim: The paper gives a unified affine-to-linear SVD formulation for the QK, OV, MLP-input, and MLP-output maps by folding each bias into a constant coordinate.
key_findings.evidence: For QK, the augmented bilinear matrix contains b_Q b_K^T, b_Q W_K^T, W_Q b_K^T, and W_Q W_K^T blocks. The OV map augments the attention-weighted residual with 1 and includes b_V W_O plus the per-head output bias. MLP input and output projections likewise stack their biases above their weight matrices. SVD then expresses every augmented map as a sum of rank-one sigma_i u_i v_i^T terms. This is an exact algebraic reparameterization before truncation or masking.

anchors.section: 2 A Unified Linear View of Transformer Components
MLP Layer Reformulation and unified dimensions

key_findings.claim: For OV and both MLP maps, the learned mask routes clean and corrupted activations through complementary singular subspaces rather than pruning the complement out of the computation.
key_findings.evidence: The reconstructed OV, MLP-input, and MLP-output matrices vertically concatenate U Sigma M V^T with U Sigma (I-M) V^T. Algorithm 1's helper h concatenates clean and corrupted activations so directions selected by M receive clean-run values and complementary directions receive fixed corrupted-run values. Both contributions remain in the forward pass. Calling the result a model that 'retains only' directions, reports them as 'pruned,' or treats its sparsity as standalone model compression is therefore misleading: the experiment is a task-corruption-conditioned clean-versus-corrupt routing attribution unless the complement is later removed and separately evaluated, which is not reported.

key_findings.claim: QK directions are treated asymmetrically: only the masked clean kernel is retained, while OV and MLP complements carry corrupted activations.
key_findings.evidence: The authors omit U Sigma (I-M) V^T for QK because two complementary similarity maps would be combined under one softmax and could create spurious correlations. Their own mixed-score example shows why corrupted QK similarity could drive a genuinely useful direction's mask toward zero. This rationale makes the intervention operationally coherent, but means mask values across QK, OV, and MLP do not have a uniform causal meaning and the full network is not simply one globally pruned set of SVD terms.

key_findings.claim: Direction masks are extremely sparse by the paper's measures, but the reported task preservation is incomplete and does not by itself establish a faithful sparse subnetwork.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports relative/full sparsity of 91.32/98.66% for IOI, 95.21/99.26% for Greater Than, and 96.81/99.51% for Gender Pronoun, with KL 0.21+/-0.02, 0.23+/-0.03, and 0.13+/-0.01. IOI accuracy falls from 0.79+/-0.05 to 0.70+/-0.07 and exact match is 0.77+/-0.06; Greater Than exact match is only 0.33+/-0.06; Gender Pronoun accuracy is 0.75+/-0.04 versus 0.77+/-0.04 and exact match 0.86+/-0.07. Because OV/MLP complements still use corrupt activations and the uncertainty source is undefined, these numbers show sparse routing under a particular corruption and objective, not task-complete compression.

key_findings.claim: The asserted superiority to random and top-k singular-value selection is not auditable from the pinned paper because the promised quantitative baseline results are absent.
key_findings.evidence: The main text states that learned directions have substantially lower KL divergence than top-k magnitude or random SVD baselines and directs the reader to Appendix B for quantitative details. Across all Appendix B subsections, figures, and tables through page 33, no random-selection or top-k result, protocol, k-matching rule, repeat count, or numerical comparison appears. Table 1 contains only the learned method and the full-model accuracy column.

anchors.section: Appendix B opening and experimental details

key_findings.claim: High QK mask values correlate visually with previously known IOI circuit heads, but no statistical test or component-matched control establishes selective recovery.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 1 and 7 group or highlight Name Mover, Backup Name Mover, Negative Name Mover, and S-Inhibition heads and show higher average mask activation than other categories; Figure 7 has no numeric table, uncertainty, permutation test, thresholded recovery metric, or adjustment for singular spectra, head depth, prior selection, or number of directions. The analysis begins from head roles discovered by earlier component-level causal work, so it validates qualitative alignment rather than independently discovering the circuit or proving the masked directions mediate it.

anchors.section: R2 comparison to known IOI circuits

key_findings.claim: Selected directions inside IOI head 9.6 have intelligible attention-score patterns, but their labels are post-hoc descriptions without direction-level causal ablation.
key_findings.evidence: S7 separates entities at +3.52+/-1.42 from actions at -4.44+/-0.68, S28 assigns larger scores to named entities than many function words, and S1 strongly favors the first token. Their learned mask values are 0.64, 0.97, and 0.53. These patterns are concrete and repeat across displayed samples, yet the paper supplies no annotation protocol, blinded labeling, random-direction comparison, held-out classification of the proposed concepts, or intervention removing each direction and measuring IOI loss. Orthogonality of an SVD basis also does not make the described functions statistically or causally independent.

key_findings.claim: The extended IOI interpretations broaden the catalog of apparent subfunctions, but remain selected descriptive examples rather than an exhaustive or independently validated decomposition.
key_findings.evidence: For head 9.9, the appendix assigns S1/S7 sequence-start roles, S51 an early-name affinity, and S16 repeat inhibition with repeated-entity scores 2.31 points lower. For head 10.0, it describes S6 as entity/location filtering, S3 as function-word suppression, S7 as entity/action separation, and S20 as preferring the indirect object in 54-59% of cases. No total number of inspected directions, selection rule, multiple-comparison correction, alternative interpretations, or effect on end-task behavior is provided.

key_findings.claim: Greater-Than results contain direct negative evidence that a visually salient rank-one attention pattern need not receive a task-important mask.
key_findings.evidence: In head 9.1, S31 and S3 make the target year token the maximum-attended token in 100% and 99.8% of prompts with masks 1.0, but S26 does so in 90.9% with mask 3.29e-5. In head 6.9, S2 reaches 100% with mask 1.0, while S7 reaches 83.3% with mask 6.81e-6 and S29 reaches 50% with mask 1.14e-5. Thus an easily interpreted local score pattern can be irrelevant under the learned global routing objective, and the paper does not reconcile this mismatch with claims that interpretable directions are the functional ones.

key_findings.claim: Claims of universal S1 and S7 primitives across tasks are supported only by selected plots and prose, not a systematic cross-task invariance analysis.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 10-11 show one instance each for head 9.6: S1 as a start-of-sequence detector and S7 as an entity/action separator. The discussion extrapolates these to reusable universal composite functionalities, but does not report task-by-direction matrices, effect sizes across datasets, sampling criteria, failure counts, mask stability, or tests in another model. Singular index numbers are component-local and do not themselves align a semantic axis across distinct matrices.

key_findings.claim: A 'logit receptor' is exactly the right singular residual direction projected through the unembedding, with an input-dependent scalar coefficient; the algebra is correct but does not alone identify a new causal unit.
key_findings.evidence: For an OV map, the head output is sum_k sigma_k (nu^T u_k) v_k^T. Multiplying v_k^T by W_U gives a fixed vocabulary-logit vector, while nu^T u_k varies with the attention-weighted input. This factorization cleanly separates a fixed output direction from its scalar use. However, any fixed residual direction has a fixed unembedding projection, and for heads before the last layer this direct projection omits layer normalization and all downstream attention/MLP transformations. Semantic top tokens in v_k^T W_U are therefore a useful descriptor, not proof the intact network reads that direction as an autonomous receptor.

anchors.section: B.2 From Singular Vectors to Logit Receptors

key_findings.claim: Gender-conditioned activations distinguish useful from merely token-aligned OV axes in the selected examples, showing that singular magnitude or token projection alone is insufficient.
key_findings.evidence: L9.H7.SV1 has mask 1.00, singular value 8.87, masculine top tokens, and activation +0.115+/-0.027 on 'he' contexts versus -0.453+/-0.032 on 'she.' L10.H9.SV0 has mask 1.00, singular value 9.15, feminine tokens, and -0.273+/-0.041 versus +0.652+/-0.038. By contrast L11.H7.SV0 has the largest listed singular value, 22.07, and feminine tokens but mask 1.3e-5 because activations are +0.755+/-0.020 and +0.774+/-0.018 across the two contexts. This supports task-conditioned selection, though the table is a hand-selected subset and lacks held-out classification controls.

key_findings.claim: Amplified opposite-gender mean swaps can force near-complete pronoun reversal, but the strongest headline result requires an intervention up to twenty times the native singular value.
key_findings.evidence: For 150 masculine prompts, swapping all selected directions changes mean correct-minus-opposite logit from +2.53+/-1.48 to -1.10+/-0.83 at scale 1 with 83.5% he-to-she flips, and to -42.31+/-8.57 at scale 20 with 100% flips. For 156 feminine prompts, scale 1 changes +2.84+/-2.12 to +1.01+/-0.96 with only 4.7% she-to-he flips; scale 2 gives 67%, and scales 5-20 give 100% among baseline-she predictions, ending at -40.82+/-15.44. The dramatic symmetric result is therefore high-gain steering rather than a natural-scale necessity test.

key_findings.claim: The gender intervention proves that the chosen residual steering vectors can control final logits, but not that the original attention heads causally mediate their predictions through those singular directions.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 2 computes each source head's SVD activation, replaces it with an opposite-gender mean, rescales sigma, sums Delta R, and adds that vector directly to the final residual stream before final LayerNorm and unembedding. This bypasses the head's original layer and every intervening component; the paper does not patch the activation at its source, remove the direction, measure causal completeness/necessity, compare equal-norm random or token-matched directions, or audit non-gender logits and fluency. A vector designed from v^T W_U is expected to steer logits when injected immediately before W_U, so this is narrower causal evidence than the paper claims.

key_findings.claim: The training schedule is internally contradictory: the hyperparameter table says 15 epochs while the adjacent prose says a maximum of 150 epochs.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 lists batch size 64, number of epochs 15, learning rate 1e-2, weight decay 1e-9, and L1 weight 1.5e-4. The paragraph immediately below says mask optimization and probing train for a maximum of 150 epochs with early stopping. No per-task stopping epoch or correction resolves which value generated Table 1.

key_findings.claim: The definition of full sparsity has a denominator mismatch with the claimed all-component analysis.
key_findings.evidence: Relative sparsity thresholds learned masks at 1e-2 within N_learnable directions. Appendix B.6 defines full sparsity using N_total as all singular directions 'across all OV projections,' even though Table 1 and the method optimize QK, OV, MLP-input, and MLP-output masks and describe full-matrix compression. The paper does not state whether the displayed full sparsity is OV-only, uses an unstated all-map denominator, or combines unlike matrix sizes, so 98.66-99.51% full sparsity is not reproducibly defined.

key_findings.claim: Evidence is restricted to one 124M-parameter base model and three templated tasks built around circuits already characterized in prior work.
key_findings.evidence: Every experiment freezes GPT-2 Small and uses IOI, Greater Than, or a binary Gender Pronoun template with train/validation/test sizes 1000/200/1000, 2000/500/2000, and 1000/155/307. The author discussion explicitly defers larger models such as Phi or LLaMA, real-world settings, and targeted causal validation. Results do not establish model-agnostic scalability, discovery in unknown circuits, instruction-tuned behavior, naturalistic concepts, or cross-model stability.

anchors.section: A Datasets and B.1 Compute Resources

method.core_idea: Replace component-level circuit units with rank-one directions from the SVD of bias-augmented transformer weight maps, then learn task-conditioned diagonal masks that decide which directions receive clean versus corrupted activations while preserving the original model's next-token distribution and encouraging sparse selection.
method.mechanism: Biases are folded into QK, OV, MLP-input, and MLP-output matrices via a constant coordinate. Each W_aug is decomposed as U Sigma V^T and receives a mask M in [0,1]. QK uses only U Sigma M V^T on clean activations. OV and both MLP projections concatenate U Sigma M V^T with U Sigma (I-M) V^T so clean and fixed corrupted-run activations feed complementary subspaces. Frozen GPT-2 Small masks minimize KL[p(y|x) || p_M(y|x)] plus lambda times the mask L1 norm. The learned axes are inspected through rank-one QK attention scores and OV right-singular-vector projections through the unembedding. Selected gender-sensitive OV axes are further tested by replacing their scalar activations with opposite-gender means, scaling their singular values, and adding the summed residual delta immediately before the final LayerNorm/unembedding.
assumptions: The SVD basis of an augmented weight matrix is a meaningful functional coordinate system rather than merely a parameterization chosen by Euclidean geometry.
Orthogonality of singular vectors corresponds sufficiently to separable computation despite softmax, GeLU, residual addition, LayerNorm, and cross-layer interaction.
Singular directions are stable and identifiable when singular values are close or repeated; no spectrum-gap or basis-stability analysis is supplied.
The scale of the appended constant coordinate is canonical, even though changing units on that coordinate changes the bias-augmented SVD basis.
Axis-aligned diagonal masks can recover a task subspace even if the relevant computation is a rotation or combination within a near-degenerate singular subspace.
The selected corruption changes the task label while preserving nuisance structure and does not create shortcuts that dominate mask learning.
Routing corrupted activations through complementary OV/MLP directions is a faithful proxy for removing or deeming those directions unnecessary.
KL agreement with the original next-token distribution on templated examples captures the behavior needed to call a selected subspace faithful.
A fixed threshold of 1e-2 converts continuous masks into meaningful active/inactive directions across maps with different ranks and scales.
Known IOI and Greater-Than heads are suitable validation targets even though selecting them after prior circuit discovery can inflate interpretability.
Human descriptions of selected rank-one attention patterns correspond to reproducible functions without a formal ontology or independent annotators.
The direct unembedding projection of an intermediate residual direction reflects how the intact downstream network uses it.
Adding a constructed delta at the final residual stream tests the causal role of a source-head direction rather than only the steerability of its unembedding-aligned vector.
Binary templated he/she contexts are an adequate test of gender-related semantics and not primarily a narrow lexical/classification artifact.
One frozen GPT-2 Small model and three synthetic/templated tasks support the proposed model-agnostic and general directional perspective.

techniques.role: Folds affine biases into constant-coordinate matrices so attention and MLP maps share one SVD treatment.
Expresses each augmented component as ordered orthogonal rank-one mappings without initially truncating nonzero directions.
Learns a diagonal coefficient in [0,1] for every retained singular direction.
Feeds clean activations through selected OV/MLP axes and fixed corrupted activations through their complement.
Suppresses QK rank-one kernels without a corrupted complementary similarity map.
Balances reconstruction of the frozen model's predictive distribution against sparse mask activation.
Visualizes [1,x_i] sigma_k u_k v_k^T [1,x_j]^T to assign semantic or positional roles to QK axes.
Projects OV right singular vectors through W_U to associate each fixed residual axis with vocabulary preferences.
Compares nu^T u activation distributions across masculine and feminine prompt contexts.
Replaces selected direction activations with their opposite-gender empirical means.
Scales intervention deltas from one to twenty times native singular values to test output steerability.
Adds the aggregate SVD-direction delta immediately before final LayerNorm and unembedding.
Counts directions with learned mask above 1e-2 to report relative and purported full sparsity.

evaluations.setting: Frozen GPT-2 Small direction-mask training on IOI (1000/200/1000 train/validation/test), Greater Than (2000/500/2000), and Gender Pronoun (1000/155/307), with clean and corrupted runs.
evaluations.metric: Relative/full sparsity, KL divergence to the original model, pruned versus full accuracy where defined, and exact match; the source of the plus/minus variation is not specified.
evaluations.baseline: Original frozen GPT-2 distribution/accuracy. Random and top-k SVD baselines are claimed but no numerical results or protocols appear in the pinned paper.

evaluations.setting: IOI QK mask maps over all GPT-2 Small heads, grouped post hoc by circuit roles from Wang et al. and ACDC.
evaluations.metric: Visual mask intensity and average mask by known head category.
evaluations.result: Known Name Mover, Backup/Negative Name Mover, and S-Inhibition categories appear to have higher masks than many other heads, but no numeric recovery score, error bars, null distribution, or significance test is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Prior component-level IOI circuit labels and uncategorized/other heads.

evaluations.setting: Selected QK singular directions in IOI heads 9.6, 9.9, and 10.0.
evaluations.metric: Rank-one unnormalized attention-score statistics and qualitative token-role patterns.
evaluations.result: Head 9.6 S7 separates entities +3.52+/-1.42 from actions -4.44+/-0.68; S1, S7, and S28 receive masks 0.53, 0.64, and 0.97. Additional selected axes are described as sequence starts, name salience, repeat inhibition, function-word suppression, and partial indirect-object preference.
evaluations.baseline: Whole-head role labels from the prior IOI circuit; no random-direction, annotator, or direction-ablation baseline.

evaluations.setting: Selected QK directions from known Greater-Than heads 9.1, 6.9, and 5.5.
evaluations.metric: Mean rank-one attention score and frequency with which the target year token has the highest score, alongside learned mask value.
evaluations.result: Head 9.1 S31/S3 select the target year in 100/99.8% with masks 1, while S26 reaches 90.9% with mask 3.29e-5. Head 6.9 S2 reaches 100% with mask 1, while S7 reaches 83.3% with mask 6.81e-6. Several interpretable local patterns therefore do not align with mask importance.
evaluations.baseline: Known Greater-Than component circuit and other selected directions; no end-task direction ablation.

evaluations.setting: Selected OV singular directions on binary Gender Pronoun prompts.
evaluations.metric: Mask, singular value, top tokens in v^T W_U, conditional mean+/-standard-deviation activation, and he-minus-she activation difference.
evaluations.result: High-mask masculine and feminine directions show strong conditional separation, while L11.H7.SV0 has sigma 22.07 and feminine top tokens but mask 1.3e-5 because its activations are nearly equal across contexts.
evaluations.baseline: Large/token-aligned but non-discriminative directions within the selected table; no held-out classifier or exhaustive direction report.

evaluations.setting: Final-residual opposite-gender mean-swap interventions on 150 masculine and 156 feminine prompts, with singular-value scaling from 1 to 20.
evaluations.metric: Correct-minus-opposite pronoun logit and recoverable baseline-pronoun flip rate.
evaluations.result: All-direction masculine swaps move +2.53+/-1.48 to -1.10+/-0.83 at 1x with 83.5% he-to-she flips and -42.31+/-8.57 at 20x with 100%. Feminine swaps move +2.84+/-2.12 to +1.01+/-0.96 at 1x with 4.7% she-to-he flips and -40.82+/-15.44 at 20x with 100% among baseline-she predictions.
evaluations.baseline: Unintervened logits and partial-direction swaps; absent equal-norm random, token-matched, source-layer patching, and side-effect controls.

evaluations.result: One NVIDIA A40 48GB, PyTorch 2.1, Transformers 4.35, TransformerLens, AdamW, batch 64, learning rate 1e-2, weight decay 1e-9, L1 1.5e-4; Table 3 says 15 epochs while prose says maximum 150 with early stopping.
evaluations.baseline: No runtime, per-task stopping epoch, seed count, or compute comparison to component-, SAE-, transcoder-, or sparse-decomposition methods.

limitations: Author-stated: some discovered directions remain difficult to interpret fully.
Author-stated: diagonal masking cannot represent every functional subspace and L0 or other selection methods remain future work.
Author-stated: targeted interventions are still needed to validate the causal contributions of discovered components.
Author-stated: generalization to larger models such as Phi or LLaMA and to real-world settings is untested.
All evidence comes from one frozen GPT-2 Small checkpoint and three synthetic or templated tasks whose component circuits were already studied.
OV and MLP complementary directions receive corrupted activations rather than being removed, so reported sparsity is not evidence for a deployable compressed subnetwork.
QK mask semantics differ from OV/MLP mask semantics because only QK drops the complement.
Corruption construction for the added Greater-Than and Gender Pronoun data is not specified precisely enough to reproduce or audit task/nuisance preservation.
The claimed random and top-k SVD baseline advantage has no numerical result, protocol, repeat count, or table in the pinned version.
Table 3's 15 epochs contradicts adjacent prose specifying a maximum of 150 epochs.
The source of reported standard deviations, number of seeds/runs, early-stopping outcomes, and uncertainty over masks is not defined.
Appendix B.6 defines the full-sparsity denominator using OV directions despite an all-QK/OV/MLP method and table, making the full percentage ambiguous.
Near-zero singular directions are removed before optimization based on an approximately 1e-6 KL cost, but the threshold, per-map counts, and taskwise reconstruction details are absent.
A fixed 1e-2 mask threshold is not justified or sensitivity-tested.

SVD directions are not unique under repeated singular values and can be unstable under close singular values, seeds, finetuning, reparameterization, or small weight perturbations; no stability audit is reported.
Bias augmentation depends on the arbitrary scaling of the appended constant coordinate, so the resulting singular basis is not invariant to units.
Orthogonal rank-one weight terms need not implement independent subfunctions after attention softmax, GeLU, LayerNorm, residual mixing, or cross-layer composition.
The interpretation examples are selected manually without a declared selection denominator, annotation rubric, blinded raters, random-direction control, or systematic concept metric.
Known circuit heads are used as analysis targets, so the paper does not show discovery of a previously unknown circuit from directions alone.
The 'universal' S1/S7 patterns are illustrated with selected examples rather than quantified across all tasks, heads, directions, and models.
Direct unembedding of an intermediate OV direction ignores the downstream transformer and can misstate its intact-network effect.

Gender interventions are injected into the final residual stream rather than the source head and are amplified up to 20x, so they establish steering sufficiency more directly than native causal mediation.
No equal-norm random, token-matched, opposite-sign, or non-gender direction control distinguishes special receptor structure from generic final-logit steering.
No evaluation measures intervention side effects on other vocabulary logits, perplexity, syntax, semantic preservation, calibration, or unrelated tasks.
The Gender Pronoun task is binary, templated, and socially reductive; results should not be generalized to gender representation or bias broadly.
The paper does not establish computational scalability: one A40 is named, but SVD, activation caching, mask parameter count, wall time, and memory by model size are not reported.
failure_modes: A learned mask can exploit artifacts of the clean/corrupt pair and identify corruption-discriminating rather than task-mediating directions.
OV/MLP complement routing can make a low mask mean 'use the corrupted activation here,' not 'this direction is unnecessary.'
A direction can show a clean semantic attention pattern yet have a near-zero learned mask, as Greater-Than S26 and S7 demonstrate.
A large singular value and interpretable vocabulary projection can be behaviorally nondiscriminative, as L11.H7.SV0 demonstrates.
Near-degenerate singular spectra can rotate or swap basis axes, destroying semantic labels while leaving the represented subspace unchanged.
A task-relevant rotated combination of singular directions can be missed or split because only diagonal axis-aligned masks are learned.
Scaling the constant bias coordinate or an equivalent model reparameterization can change the augmented SVD and apparent subfunctions without changing behavior.
Post-hoc semantic naming can overfit a few prompts or selected tokens and fail on held-out contexts.
Direct-logit projection can assign a compelling token label to a direction that downstream layers normally cancel, rotate, gate, or never use.
High-gain final-residual injection can flip predictions through an unnatural shortcut while perturbing many unreported logits and unrelated behaviors.
Sparsity percentages can be overstated or irreproducible when the denominator mixes only OV with QK and MLP selections.
Early stopping under the unresolved 15-versus-150-epoch schedule can materially alter masks, sparsity, and semantic rankings.
A sparse reconstruction can retain low KL while losing exact task behavior, as the 0.33 Greater-Than exact-match result illustrates.
reusable_insights: Fold affine biases explicitly before decomposing a component when the bias participates in the behavior under study; also test sensitivity to the constant-coordinate scale.
Separate a subspace's fixed output direction from its input-dependent scalar activation; token alignment alone does not imply contextual use.
Use task-conditioned activation differences to distinguish high-variance or high-singular-value axes from behaviorally discriminative ones.
Treat singular directions as a coordinate system for hypotheses, not automatically as independent mechanisms; validate the subspace under rotations and weight perturbations.
If complementary directions carry corrupted activations, call the procedure clean/corrupt routing or attribution and evaluate a genuinely pruned model separately before claiming compression.
Define consistent intervention semantics across QK, OV, and MLP maps or report their mask values as different quantities.
Always publish random, top-k magnitude, and matched-rank baselines when a learned spectral selection is claimed to find special axes.
A direction-level interpretation should include held-out concept prediction, random-direction controls, source-site ablation/patching, and end-task effect rather than only selected attention plots.
Visual salience and task importance can disagree; report both positive and negative examples such as high-attention/low-mask directions.
For causal steering, intervene at the source component first, then trace downstream propagation; final-residual injection answers a different sufficiency question.
Sweep intervention norm from native scale and compare equal-norm controls before using large amplified flips as causal evidence.
Report sparsity numerators and denominators separately for every map family, threshold sensitivity, retained ranks, and actual parameter/FLOP savings.
Audit basis stability across seeds, checkpoints, fine-tuning, sign alignment, singular-value gaps, and rotations within degenerate subspaces before assigning persistent semantic names.
Distinguish circuit discovery from refinement: reanalyzing known heads can validate resolution but does not demonstrate blind recovery of a new circuit.
open_questions: What exact clean/corrupt transformations were used for Greater Than and Gender Pronoun, and do alternate valid corruptions recover the same masks?
Do the learned masks remain stable across optimization seeds, data resamples, mask initializations, epoch budgets, and the unresolved 15-versus-150 schedule?
Are semantic subspaces stable under close-singular-value rotations, sign alignment, small weight perturbations, model reparameterizations, and changes to the bias-coordinate scale?
What happens when the complement is truly zeroed and the resulting sparse model is evaluated end to end, rather than supplied with corrupted activations?
Can a learned low-dimensional rotated projector outperform the diagonal SVD mask at equal rank and KL?
Where are the numerical random and top-k SVD baselines promised in the main text, and do they remain inferior at matched active direction count and compute?
How should full sparsity be computed jointly across QK, OV, MLP-input, and MLP-output maps, and what parameter/FLOP savings result?
Do direction masks recover an unknown held-out circuit without first selecting heads from prior mechanistic work?
Can independent annotators or automated concept datasets reproduce the S1, S7, S28, and other semantic labels on held-out prompts?
What is the causal necessity and completeness of each interpreted direction when patched or ablated at its original head/layer?
Do logit-receptor labels survive downstream processing, or does a causal tracing analysis show cancellation and rotation before the final layer?
Do native-scale source-layer mean swaps flip gender predictions, and how do they compare to equal-norm random and token-matched directions?
What non-target tokens, perplexity, grammaticality, and unrelated tasks change under the 5x-20x final-residual intervention?
Does the framework scale computationally and semantically to larger instruction-tuned models, natural tasks, and circuits not defined by templated token positions?
Can the apparent recurring primitives be aligned at the subspace level across different heads and models rather than equating component-local singular indices such as S1?

competitive_landscape.title: Talking Heads: Understanding Inter-layer Communication in Transformer Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest acknowledged spectral antecedent: it analyzes low-rank singular-vector channels through which attention heads communicate across layers.
competitive_landscape.difference: Talking Heads focuses on inter-component communication through attention value/output geometry across two language models and includes causal interventions and weight edits; Beyond Components extends the affine SVD lens inside QK, OV, and both MLP projections with task masks. The extension in component coverage is real, but its causal validation is weaker and should be compared directly to the prior channel-level interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Understanding the Nature of Attention with Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Close pre-publication competitor decomposing attention into fine-grained low-rank sparse functional units rather than treating heads as atomic.
competitive_landscape.difference: The low-rank sparse decomposition replaces multi-head self-attention with learned sparse low-rank units and evaluates larger Llama-3.1-8B circuits and reconstruction against SAE-style alternatives; Beyond Components uses the fixed SVD basis of frozen GPT-2 weights, folds in biases, and adds MLP maps. This is an important omitted direct comparator because it challenges the breadth and novelty of the general 'below components' framing while differing in learned versus intrinsic axes.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct fine-grained attention-output interpretability competitor using learned sparse features instead of singular directions.
competitive_landscape.difference: The SAE work decomposes attention outputs into sparse activation features, studies models up to 2B parameters, reports widespread head polysemanticity, and performs IOI causal analysis. Beyond Components obtains orthogonal directions directly from weights and spans QK plus MLPs without training a dictionary. The tradeoff is intrinsic/exact spectral axes versus empirically sparse nonlinear features with stronger feature-level validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct competitor for decomposing MLP computation into interpretable subcomponent feature circuits, including the Greater-Than task.
competitive_landscape.difference: Transcoders learn a sparse nonlinear replacement whose features and feature-to-feature edges support circuit analysis; Beyond Components retains frozen weights and uses their orthogonal singular rank-one maps across both attention and MLPs. Transcoders offer a more expressive learned basis and circuit graph, while the SVD method is simpler and exact at the matrix level before masking.

competitive_landscape.title: Singular Vectors of Attention Heads Align with Features
competitive_landscape.relationship: Subsequent direct analysis of when attention-head singular vectors correspond to true model features.
competitive_landscape.difference: The later work gives theoretical conditions and controlled ground-truth experiments for feature alignment in QK singular vectors, showing that alignment is conditional rather than automatic. Beyond Components supplies broader empirical QK/OV/MLP case studies but assumes singular axes are natural functional coordinates. This later result is the most precise primary-source test of that core assumption.

competitive_landscape.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
competitive_landscape.relationship: Methodological counterpoint on the causal validity of behavior-changing subspace interventions.
competitive_landscape.difference: The illusion paper shows that subspace patching can produce the expected behavior through a dormant or unintended pathway and argues for additional causal-faithfulness checks. Beyond Components infers causal building blocks from final-residual SVD-vector injection, precisely the kind of sufficiency result that can outstrip mediation evidence. Equal-norm controls, source-site patching, and completeness tests are therefore decisive missing comparisons.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 Small
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational IOI circuit source whose head categories and task structure are reused as ground truth for the paper's directional analysis.
competitive_landscape.difference: The IOI work identifies a 26-head, seven-class circuit with causal faithfulness, completeness, and minimality analyses at component level. Beyond Components refines selected known heads into SVD axes but does not repeat those causal criteria direction by direction. Its novelty is resolution below the known circuit, not discovery of the underlying IOI algorithm or heads.

competitive_landscape.title: How does GPT-2 compute greater-than? Interpreting mathematical abilities in a pre-trained language model
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational Greater-Than circuit source whose task, heads, and functional interpretation are reused for the SVD case study.
competitive_landscape.difference: The prior paper identifies and causally analyzes the GPT-2 Small Greater-Than circuit; Beyond Components decomposes already implicated heads 6.9, 9.1, and 5.5 into rank-one QK score patterns. The later decomposition exposes finer geometry, but without direction ablations it does not supersede the prior mechanistic circuit evidence.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a model-agnostic directional interpretability perspective that goes beyond monolithic heads and MLPs by decomposing every major affine transformer map into orthogonal singular subfunctions, learning sparse task-relevant masks, discovering multiple interpretable functions within known heads, and identifying controllable fixed logit receptors as causal computational building blocks.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper contributes an explicit bias-augmented QK/OV/MLP SVD formulation and one unified mask implementation across GPT-2 Small. Sparse masks retain partial distribution/task agreement on IOI, Greater Than, and Gender Pronoun; selected rank-one QK patterns admit plausible positional, entity, action, repetition, and number-token descriptions; selected OV directions separate gender contexts; and amplified final-residual activation swaps strongly control pronoun logits. Yet OV/MLP complements are routed from corrupt activations rather than pruned, promised random/top-k numbers are absent, direction semantics are manually selected, full-sparsity and epoch definitions conflict, and the intervention bypasses the original circuit.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The clearest novelty is engineering and exposition: a single bias-aware spectral coordinate system spanning QK, OV, MLP input, and MLP output, coupled to task-conditioned masks and vocabulary projection. The general idea that components contain low-rank/sparse substructure, attention heads communicate through singular directions, and MLP/attention outputs can be decomposed into interpretable features is established by close prior work. 'Logit receptors' restate the exact fact that a fixed residual direction has a fixed unembedding image; the useful addition is conditional scalar analysis, not a new kind of neuron. Claims of pruning, independent subfunctions, universal primitives, and native causal mediation exceed the evidence. Durable novelty is therefore a promising integrated diagnostic lens and set of case studies, not a validated decomposition of transformer computation into stable causal atoms.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text audit of the exact cached 33-page PDF for arXiv 2511.20273v1, marked in the paper as NeurIPS 2025. The unversioned pinned source locator is https://export.arxiv.org/pdf/2511.20273; PDF SHA-256 f65edaadeae27f9fb556c0a2716272a5b75af19cc5332abd37c8ea581420ee65 and extracted-text SHA-256 531eb8074f495f9c7fb44bcba6730b330d4bcc3774311932550a5dc0a47af08a match the full-text index, with all 33 pages present. PDF metadata identifies https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20273v1, the official current record was checked on 2026-08-23 and remained v1, and bytes fetched from https://export.arxiv.org/pdf/2511.20273v1 matched the pinned PDF hash. Every extracted page was read, including all references, Appendix A, Appendix B.1-B.7, equations, algorithms, tables, captions, and otherwise sparse figure pages; PDF renderings of pages 5-8 and 22-25 were inspected directly to confirm the complementary routing equations, Algorithm 1, Table 1, selected receptor rows, intervention algorithm, and Tables 5-6. Competitors were checked against current versioned official arXiv records on 2026-08-23. The audit preserves four material unresolved issues: routing is described as pruning, the random/top-k quantitative comparison is absent, Table 3 says 15 epochs while prose says 150, and full sparsity names an OV-only denominator despite all-component claims. This is a primary review, not an independent secondary verification.
